## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `--exclude` flag needs an `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` environment-variable default, because the project's CLI flag policy requires one for every new flag under `cli/`. The filtering logic matches the documented behavior, which is to compare each file's basename against each pattern, and the added tests cover it.

## Changes
The pull request adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` option. Files whose basename matches any pattern are logged and skipped in `collect`, and `main` passes the option through. It also documents the flag in `docs/flags.md`, adds tests for parsing, filtering and archive contents, and adds a text fixture under `tests/fixtures/`.

(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Default `--exclude` from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` — `--exclude` is added with `default=[]` and does not read an `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` environment variable, so a CI job that sets `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` still archives every file. This breaks `.agents/skills/cli-flags/reference.md:5`: "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable". — CI pipelines that set options through the environment, as the policy expects, cannot exclude files. — Fix: Seed the default from `os.environ.get("ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE")`, choose and document a separator for multiple patterns in `docs/flags.md`, and extend `test_exclude_defaults_to_nothing` to cover the environment case.
